key_insight: Shallow neural networks learn low-frequency, sinusoidal-like components first because the gradient-descent dynamics matrix has a graded structure whose eigenvalues decay and eigenvectors align with orthogonal-polynomial Fourier modes.
engineering_relevance: This framework gives a more general theory of spectral bias that can help engineers predict training dynamics across activation functions and data distributions, not just in Fourier-domain toy settings.
method: Expand network outputs as a general Fourier series in an orthogonal polynomial basis.
Derive gradient-descent dynamics for the series coefficients as an ODE system with dynamics matrix H.
Analyze H's eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes to explain why smooth sinusoidal components emerge first.
evidence_signal: The paper is theoretical, using asymptotic analysis of the dynamics matrix H rather than new experimental data in the abstract.
watch_item: The framework is analytical and depends on the polynomial-basis approximation, so practical validation and numerical stability may vary for specific architectures and datasets.
paper_title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
